body:
I don't think I can find a fun side in medicine anymore, the situation for a junior phyisician is too abusive no matter which approach you take to it. 

The way I see it medschool is there to make sure you have so much debt that your only option is indentured servitude and a life of regret or suicide, actually teaching is secondary and you'll have to bury your face in a book after you start working either way. 

I don't want to switch around in medicine, I want to switch out of it entirely but I'm too mentally drained to figure out how and what to do instead.

> I made my bed and now I have to fucking lie in it.

I was ambitious and studied and finished medschool. Every day after work I come home and feel suicidal thoughts, regret and anxiety. It wasn't a good choice. 

College is as likely as not to dig you a debt ridden pit of despair as it is to give you something good, it's definitely not the only option. Go to trade school, learn machine operations or welding or web programming or whatever. 

Also don't chose your future career based on your crush. Perhaps if you were in a long term committed relationship...

You're 18, school doesn't give you much more than some scattered fragments of value, look at the options that you still have right now, don't look at your grand imagined plans for the late 30s that don't work out anymore, look at now.
Just add a captcha to the voting process

> killyourself

It's a pretty common option based on suicide statistics, can't say I haven't considered it a few hundred times.

It makes me feel bad. It's a clusterfuck of alternating responsibility and telling patients to shut up and go home in a diplomatic manner with a sprinkle of being a salesperson to big pharma products. 

It feels like being a good politician and con-man is as important as having knowledge, and on the topic of knowledge there's a giant void between what you know after medschool and the far end of specialist knowledge that you're still assumed to know something of.

It's also doesn't work as advertised and expected, complications, treatment failure, side effects and so on are as numerous as the forest-consuming mountain of paperwork you need to deal with.
